## Trial `dns-forwarding-almalinux9__aSKXR6J`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes of the task were satisfied: node1 was configured with PowerDNS Recursor to authoritatively answer inventory.internal with node2's private address (10.100.11.11) and forward all other queries to upstream resolvers (1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9), and node2/node3 were reconfigured via nmcli to use node1 as their DNS server, with resolution of both internal and external names verified from both nodes. The independently required provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated on all three nodes, with pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot identities, and confirmed recovery of DNS service and resolution, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is high; the only residue is a trivial /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the reboot mechanism on two nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) configured as the DNS resolver for the shared private network, answering inventory.internal with node2's address on that network
  - **Why:** node1's service dns forwarding was set with listen-address 10.100.11.10, allow-from 10.100.11.0/24, and authoritative-domain inventory.internal record A @ -> 10.100.11.11 (node2's private IP), committed and saved. pdns_recursor confirmed listening on 10.100.11.10:53 and dig from node1 resolved inventory.internal to 10.100.11.11.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-956053cc315642bd`, `cmd-8100e929fd5f49f1`, `cmd-54a3e08ad1524959`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node1 forwards all other (non-inventory.internal) DNS queries upstream
  - **Why:** name-server entries 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 were configured; dig @10.100.11.10 google.com returned real public IPs both immediately after configuration and after node1's restart, confirming forwarding works.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-54a3e08ad1524959`, `cmd-983c7c79131a4998`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 configured to resolve through node1
  - **Why:** nmcli was used on both node2 and node3 to set ipv4.dns=10.100.11.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes; resolv.conf on both nodes showed nameserver 10.100.11.10, and getent hosts on both nodes resolved inventory.internal (to 10.100.11.11) and google.com, confirming end-to-end resolution through node1.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2f21f7194b6f482d`, `cmd-a3f3634a22954b3b`, `cmd-ddc0fd1e1fc4440f`, `cmd-bd77dc6228ec4870`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated on node1, node2, node3
  - **Why:** For each node, a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-state baseline (pdns-recursor active on node1; resolv.conf/getent working on node2/node3) was captured, a reboot was acknowledged, connectivity was polled until restored, a distinct post-restart boot_id was observed, and DNS service/resolution was re-verified as healthy post-restart on all three nodes. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity observations, which independently show all three boot_ids changed (node1: ebd78841->bad09383, node2: c207ab79->ce84b78f, node3: d6298ced->92f673f7) and post-restart listening-sockets/package-health remained healthy with no failed services.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-76b992376f9a4192`, `cmd-9446833ad62b4a29`, `cmd-e3d39224e9684a08`, `cmd-983c7c79131a4998`, `cmd-a0b44b7079734be2`, `cmd-0f35f32173354e85`, `cmd-f01a17746f1b4011`, `cmd-7c7cda07433f4c99`, `cmd-6431ad871d3545f9`, `cmd-c878cb8d39f84b54`, `cmd-426a8ec351c84e77`, `cmd-7d8f129a05574993`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.920**. The executor's non-final commands were almost entirely read-only discovery (find, cat, grep, sed on VyOS template/conf_mode files) to determine the correct DNS-forwarding schema before committing config; none of these mutated state. The state-changing commands (VyOS set/commit/save on node1, nmcli con mod/con up on node2 and node3, and the three sequential native reboots) each map directly to a material task outcome or the mandatory restart protocol; no unnecessary or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were found. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log left behind on node2 and node3 by the nohup-backgrounded reboot invocation, a small, inert, non-security-relevant artifact from the required restart mechanism rather than an independent mutation, so it is treated as low-severity leftover rather than a penalized unnecessary change.
